title: ErdosProblems/505: `erdos_505` and its variants admit unbounded covering sets, whose `Metric.diam` is zero
body:
`Erdos505.erdos_505`, `erdos_505.small_dim` and `erdos_505.test_dim_one` require only `S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i` with `Metric.diam (F i) < Metric.diam S`, so taking every `F i = Set.univ` (unbounded, hence of real diameter zero) satisfies the covering conclusion, whereas Borsuk's problem concerns covers of `S` by bounded pieces of strictly smaller diameter, making `small_dim` and `test_dim_one` trivially true in every dimension and `erdos_505` false.

title: Likely misformalization in `Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood.lean`: unconditional `∏'` for conditionally convergent constant
body:
### Describe the misformalization
`FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor` in `FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood.lean:63` defines `C_P` with `∏' q : {q // q.Prime ∧ 3 ≤ q}`.

Same defect class as #5255: `∏'` is `tprod`, unconditional. Junk `1` if not `Multipliable`. Here log-factor is `O(1/q)`, `∑ 1/p` diverges, so product is conditionally convergent only in increasing-prime order. Formal constant is `0` or junk.

Permalink: `FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood.lean#L63`
Related: #5255 (Bateman-Horn), #4996 (covers =O vs ∼, not this product)

### Trivial proof/disproof
No full disproof yet, by analogy to #5255 disproof (`X²+1` vs `4X²+1` giving same `1/2`): any two constellations with same `k` but different true constants will get same junk value here.

### Suggested fix
Same as #5255: replace with `N ↦ ∏ q in Nat.primesBelow N, ...` and state `∃ C > 0, Tendsto ... (𝓝 C) ∧ ...`, or otherwise make order explicit.

`ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.lean:63` checked — `1/p(p-1)` is summable, `∏'` valid there. Only Hardy-Littlewood needs fix among the `∏'` hits.

### Additional context
Found by `grep ∏'` audit (5 hits). `lake` build not run locally — statement-only change.

title: Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood: `first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture` states `=O` where the source states `∼`, and does not require the offsets distinct
body:
## Summary

`HardyLittlewood.first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture` has two independent defects.

1. It states `=O[atTop]` where its own docstring — and Wikipedia, and Hardy–Littlewood —
   state `∼`. For admissible tuples the surviving one-sided bound is a **classical
   sieve theorem**, so the declaration no longer expresses an open problem.
2. The offsets `m` are not required to be distinct. At `m = ![0, 1, 1]` the Euler
   product diverges, Mathlib's `tprod` falls back to its junk value `1`, the constant
   collapses to `C = 4`, and the resulting bound is **false** if the twin-prime count
   has its conjectured order.

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood.lean#L61-L85

```lean
def FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  let C : ℝ :=
      2 ^ k * ∏' (q : { q : ℕ // q.Prime ∧ 3 ≤ q}),
        (1 - (Nat.numResidues q m : ℝ) / q) / (1 - 1 / q) ^ k.succ
    let π_P : ℕ → ℝ := fun n => (Nat.primeTupleCounting m n : ℝ)
    π_P =O[atTop] fun n => C * ∫ t in (2)..n, 1 / t.log ^ k.succ

/-- … Then
$$
  \pi_P(n)\sim C_P\int_2^n\frac{dt}{\log^{k+1}t}.
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) :
    FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m := by
  sorry
```

## Defect 1 — `∼` weakened to `=O`

`f ∼ g` is `f / g → 1`; `f =O[atTop] g` is a one-sided bound with an arbitrary implied
constant. Replacing the first by the second discards the entire main-term content of the
conjecture — the constant `C_P` is computed with care in the file and then made
irrelevant, since `=O` tolerates any multiple of it.

Worse, what survives is provable. For a fixed admissible constellation with distinct
offsets, the Brun/Selberg sieve gives

$$\pi_P(n) \;\ll_k\; \mathfrak{S}(P)\,\frac{n}{(\log n)^{k+1}}$$

— the standard upper-bound-sieve estimate for prime `k`-tuples (Halberstam–Richert,
*Sieve Methods*, Ch. 5) — and `∫₂ⁿ dt/(log t)^{k+1} ≍ n/(log n)^{k+1}`. So the
declaration's right-hand side dominates `π_P` up to a constant by a classical theorem;
no open question is being asked. The degenerate cases are consistent with this: if the
offsets cover every residue class mod some prime `q ≥ 3` then `C = 0`, but then no `p`
is admissible either and `π_P ≡ 0`, so `=O 0` still holds.

## The constant itself is correct

Worth recording, because it is easy to suspect the `2 ^ k` prefactor. For the twin tuple
`m = ![0, 1]` (`k = 1`, `w(q) = 2` for `q ≥ 3`) the Lean's `C` evaluates to

```
2 · ∏_{3 ≤ q < 2·10⁶} (1 − 2/q)/(1 − 1/q)²  =  1.320323674
2·C₂  (twin prime constant)                 =  1.320323632…
```

The `2 ^ k` prefactor is exactly the missing `q = 2` Euler factor: all offsets `2·m i`
are even, so `w(2) = 1` and `(1 − 1/2)/(1 − 1/2)^{k+1} = 2^k`. Using residues of `m i`
rather than of `2·m i` is harmless because doubling is a bijection modulo every odd `q`.
**No defect in `C`.**

## Defect 2 — offsets are not required distinct

The theorem is `∀ m`, and nothing forbids repeats. Take `k = 2`,
**`m = ![0, 1, 1]`**. It satisfies the file's own shape conditions: `m 0 = 0` and
`∀ i ≠ 0, 0 < m i`.

* `IsPrimeConstellation m p` unfolds to "`p` and `p + 2` are both prime", since the
  index set `{p, p+2, p+2}` has only two distinct entries. Admissibility holds for every
  prime `q`: for `q ≥ 3` the image has at most 2 < q elements, and for `q = 2` both
  entries are congruent mod 2. So `Nat.primeTupleCounting m n = π₂(n)`, the count of
  twin-prime starts `p ≤ n`.
* `Nat.numResidues q m = #{0, 1} = 2` for every `q ≥ 3`, while `k.succ = 3`. Each Euler
  factor is therefore `(1 − 2/q)/(1 − 1/q)³ = 1 + 1/q + O(1/q²) > 1`, and the partial
  products **diverge** (`log` of the product is `∑ 1/q + O(1)`):

  | `Q` | `∏_{3 ≤ q ≤ Q}` |
  |---|---|
  | `10` | 1.4954 |
  | `10²` | 2.7485 |
  | `10³` | 4.0773 |
  | `10⁴` | 5.4215 |
  | `10⁵` | 6.7705 |
  | `10⁶` | 8.1224 |
  | `10⁷` | 9.4759 |

* So the family is not `Multipliable` over `ℝ`, Mathlib's `∏'` returns its junk value
  `1`, and `C = 2² · 1 = 4`.
* The asserted bound is then `π₂(n) =O[atTop] 4·∫₂ⁿ dt/(log t)³ ≍ n/(log n)³`.

This instance is **false as soon as `π₂(n) ≫ n/(log n)³`**, which is exactly what the
conjecture the declaration is named after predicts: at `m = ![0, 1]` the docstring's
`∼` gives `π₂(n) ∼ 2C₂ · n/(log n)²`. In other words the declaration, read over all `m`,
contradicts its own intended content — if the First Hardy–Littlewood conjecture is true
then `first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture` is false.

I state this as a hypothesis gap rather than a counterexample, because the falsity is
conditional: no unconditional lower bound on `π₂` is known, so `m = ![0, 1, 1]` cannot
be *proved* to refute the declaration today.

The source's `m_i` are the offsets of a constellation and are implicitly distinct
(`P = (m_1, …, m_k)` with the `p + m_i` pairwise different primes), so a hypothesis such
as `Function.Injective m` — or `StrictMono m` — belongs in `FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor`.

## The mathematics is unaffected

**Both defects are about the formalization, not about primes.** Nothing here bears on
the First Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, which remains open exactly as stated in the
source. In the four-coordinate sense: (1) the underlying conjecture is untouched;
(2) no formal solution exists; (3) the declaration is **unfaithful** to the source in
two separate ways; (4) what it literally asserts is, for distinct admissible offsets, a
classical sieve bound, and for repeated offsets a statement that the conjecture itself
would refute. Only (3) and (4) are claimed.

Note that `not_first_and_secondHardyLittlewoodConjecture` (Richards) is stated in terms
of `FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor` as an *antecedent*, so weakening that predicate
makes the Richards implication correspondingly harder to prove — it is stated with the
`=O` reading and would need revisiting alongside any fix to defect 1.

## Suggested fixes

* Defect 1: replace `π_P =O[atTop] …` with the asymptotic the docstring states, e.g.
  `atTop.Tendsto (fun n => π_P n / (C * ∫ t in (2)..n, 1 / t.log ^ k.succ)) (𝓝 1)`, or
  `Asymptotics.IsEquivalent atTop π_P (fun n => C * ∫ …)`.
* Defect 2: add an injectivity/strict-monotonicity hypothesis on `m` in
  `FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor`.

I have not opened a PR for this one: fixing defect 1 changes the statement that
`not_first_and_secondHardyLittlewoodConjecture` quantifies over, so the right shape for
that theorem should be agreed first.

## Relationship to the C₅[K₄] campaign

Found while auditing `research open` declarations in the `Wikipedia` collection for
faithfulness to their cited sources. Full derivation, the Euler-product computations,
and the duplicate search:

https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/c5-k4/blob/d8a0c47da83203e1cd2c739b383f7a436435549f/results/expansion/live-search-2026-08-15/wikipedia-scan-A-L.md

## Source/status note

Wikipedia, *First Hardy–Littlewood conjecture*, states the asymptotic relation
`π_P(n) ∼ C_P ∫₂ⁿ dt/(log t)^{k+1}` with
`C_P = 2^k ∏_{q ≥ 3 prime} [1 − w(q; m₁,…,m_k)/q] / [(1 − 1/q)^{k+1}]`, for `P` a tuple
of positive even offsets — i.e. the docstring in this file is a faithful transcription
of the source, and it is the Lean that diverges from both.

The Euler-product numbers above were computed with exact prime enumeration to `10⁷`; the
`Q = 10²` … `10⁶` rows agree with an earlier independent run of the same computation.
`git log` on this file shows no statement-level edit since creation (only docstring,
whitespace and classical-reasoning chores).

## AI assistance disclosure

This report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) for the source audit, the
numerical checks, and drafting. The submitter reviewed the declaration, the argument, and
the suggested repairs, and takes responsibility for the submission.

title: Wikipedia/Dickson: `polignac_conjecture` states the generalized twin-prime form, not de Polignac (consecutive primes), and admits `k = 0`
body:
## Summary

`Dickson.polignac_conjecture` is not de Polignac's conjecture. The source requires the
two primes to be **consecutive**; the Lean statement drops that, leaving the strictly
weaker generalised twin-prime statement. It also admits `k = 0`, where the instance
degenerates into Euclid's theorem.

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Dickson.lean#L44-L52

```lean
/--
**Polignac's conjecture**
For any integer $k$ there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 2k$ is prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem polignac_conjecture (k : ℕ) :
    Infinite {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ (p + 2 * k).Prime} := by
  sorry
```

## Divergence 1 — "consecutive" is dropped

Wikipedia, *Polignac's conjecture*:

> For any positive even number `n`, there are infinitely many prime gaps of size `n`.
> In other words: There are infinitely many cases of two **consecutive** prime numbers
> with difference `n`.

de Polignac's 1849 formulation is likewise about *"la différence de deux nombres
premiers **consécutifs**"*.

The Lean statement asks only that `p` and `p + 2k` both be prime, with no constraint on
what lies between them. For `k = 1` the two readings coincide (nothing can lie strictly
between `p` and `p + 2` except `p + 1`, which is even and `> 2`), but for `k ≥ 2` they
come apart: `(3, 7)` are both prime with gap 4 yet are not consecutive, and the weak
statement is satisfied by such pairs while de Polignac's is not.

The weak form is exactly the generalised twin-prime statement that follows from
Dickson's conjecture — which is presumably why it sits in this file under
`## Special cases`. That placement is right for the *content*; it is the **name and
docstring** that claim more than the statement delivers. Anyone searching the corpus for
de Polignac's conjecture finds this declaration and reasonably concludes it is
formalized, when the harder half is absent.

To state the source faithfully one needs consecutiveness, e.g. via `Nat.nth Nat.Prime`:

```lean
theorem polignac_conjecture (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) :
    {i : ℕ | Nat.nth Nat.Prime (i + 1) - Nat.nth Nat.Prime i = 2 * k}.Infinite
```

## Divergence 2 — `k = 0` is admitted

At `k = 0` the statement is

```lean
Infinite {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ (p + 0).Prime}   -- i.e. Infinite {p | p.Prime}
```

the infinitude of primes: a theorem of Euclid, and one already in Mathlib
(`Nat.infinite_setOf_prime`). The source restricts to `n` a *positive* even number. A
`research open` declaration should not have a proved instance; a one-token repair is
`(k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k)`.

## The mathematics is unaffected

**This is a defect in the formalization only.** Neither de Polignac's conjecture nor the
generalised twin-prime statement is being challenged here — both remain open, and the
declaration as written is not false, merely weaker than its name. In the four-coordinate
sense: (1) the underlying conjecture is untouched; (2) no formal solution exists;
(3) the declaration is **unfaithful** to its cited source; (4) what it literally asserts
is a different (weaker) open statement, with one instance, `k = 0`, that is a classical
theorem. Only (3) and (4) are claimed.

## Related work in flight

* #4673 (open) is a WIP notice from a contributor preparing *"Polignac's conjecture
  (consecutive prime gaps)"* as a **new** formalization, and #4684 (closed, asked to be
  split one-problem-per-PR) proposed `FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Polignac.lean` for it.
  That PR's own table records the distinction — *"Consecutive-gap form is strictly
  stronger for k > 2"* — so the gap identified here is already recognised. **Neither
  reports the defect in the existing `Dickson.polignac_conjecture`**, and neither renames
  it, so if that work lands the corpus would contain two differently-strong declarations
  both called Polignac's conjecture.
* A minimal resolution that does not block #4673: rename this declaration to what it
  states (e.g. `generalized_twin_primes` or `infinite_primes_add_two_mul`), reword the
  docstring, and add `0 < k`, leaving the name *Polignac* free for the consecutive-aware
  formalization.
* Note also that `k = 1` of this declaration is `TwinPrimes.twin_primes` from
  `FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/TwinPrimes.lean` (there stated with `answer(sorry) ↔`),
  so a rename would additionally make the relationship between the two files legible.

## Relationship to the C₅[K₄] campaign

Found while auditing `research open` declarations in the `Wikipedia` collection for
faithfulness to their cited sources. Full derivation and the duplicate search:

https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/c5-k4/blob/d8a0c47da83203e1cd2c739b383f7a436435549f/results/expansion/live-search-2026-08-15/wikipedia-scan-A-L.md

## Source/status note

Wikipedia's *Polignac's conjecture* article and de Polignac's original 1849 statement
both quantify over **consecutive** primes, and both require `n` positive and even; the
Lean docstring's "For any integer `k`" already drops the positivity. The conjecture is
open for every `n`; the Zhang–Maynard–Polymath bounded-gaps results give infinitely many
consecutive pairs with gap at most 246 but do not settle any single `n`.

title: Wikipedia/Koethe: `matrixOver_KotherRadical` carries an unused `{I}`/`hI`, and its docstring describes a different statement from the (correct) code
body:
## Summary

Low-severity, two small things in
`Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.matrixOver_KotherRadical`:

1. the hypotheses `{I : TwoSidedIdeal R} (hI : IsNil I)` do **not** occur in the
   conclusion — they are spurious, unlike in the two sibling declarations where the same
   `I` is the subject;
2. the docstring describes something different from (and weaker than) the code, which is
   itself correct.

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/638da20efd8eeeed2993fc2550fc596dc90c1ce8/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Koethe.lean#L74-L81

```lean
open scoped Classical in
/-- The **Köthe conjecture**: for any positive integer `n`, the Köthe radical of `R` is the matrix ideal `M_2(Nil*(R))`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 16]
theorem KotherConjecture.variants.matrixOver_KotherRadical
    {I : TwoSidedIdeal R} (hI : IsNil I) (n : Type*) [Fintype n] :
    matrix n (Nil* R) = Nil* (Matrix n n R) := by
  sorry
```

## Spurious hypotheses

`I` and `hI` appear nowhere in `matrix n (Nil* R) = Nil* (Matrix n n R)`. `I` is
implicit and otherwise unconstrained, so it can never be inferred by unification and can
only ever be supplied by hand at a use site.

This is **not** a vacuity problem: `IsNil I` is satisfiable (`I = ⊥` is nil), so the
declaration is logically equivalent to the same statement with the two binders removed —
it is not accidentally trivially true, it is just carrying dead weight. Hence "low
severity". Still worth fixing, because a reader comparing the three matrix variants sees
`(hI : IsNil I)` in all of them and reasonably assumes it plays the same role, and
because the two siblings

```lean
theorem KotherConjecture.variants.general_matrix {I : TwoSidedIdeal R} (hI : IsNil I)
    (n : Type*) [Fintype n] : IsNil (matrix n I)

theorem KotherConjecture.variants.two_by_two_matrix {I : TwoSidedIdeal R} (hI : IsNil I) :
    IsNil (matrix (Fin 2) I)
```

*do* use them.

## Docstring does not match the code

The docstring says "for any positive integer `n`, the **Köthe radical of `R`** is the
matrix ideal `M_2(Nil*(R))`". The code says `matrix n (Nil* R) = Nil* (Matrix n n R)`,
i.e. the Köthe radical of the **matrix ring** is the matrix ideal over the Köthe radical
of `R`. Two mismatches:

* `Nil*(R)` vs `Nil*(M_n(R))` on the right of the equation — the docstring names the
  wrong ring;
* `M_2` vs an arbitrary `n : Type*` `[Fintype n]` — the docstring fixes the size while
  the code quantifies over it (`M_2` is the sibling `two_by_two_matrix`).

**The code is the correct one.** Wikipedia's equivalent formulation 6 of the Köthe
conjecture reads

> For any ring `R`, the upper nilradical of `M_n(R)` is the set of matrices with entries
> from the upper nilradical of `R` for every positive integer `n`

which is exactly `matrix n (Nil* R) = Nil* (Matrix n n R)`. Only the docstring needs
changing.

## Not a defect

`n : Type*` `[Fintype n]` admits `n = Empty`; both sides then live in the trivial ring
and are equal, so the empty case is harmless and no degeneracy hides there.

## Suggested fix

```lean
open scoped Classical in
/-- The **Köthe conjecture**: for any finite index type `n`, the Köthe radical of the matrix
ring `M_n(R)` is the ideal of matrices with entries in the Köthe radical of `R`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 16]
theorem KotherConjecture.variants.matrixOver_KotherRadical (n : Type*) [Fintype n] :
    matrix n (Nil* R) = Nil* (Matrix n n R) := by
  sorry
```

I have not opened a PR: removing binders from a declaration is the kind of change a
maintainer may prefer to bundle with the file's other pending tidy-up (the namespace is
spelled `KotherConjecture` throughout, apparently a typo for `KotheConjecture`, and the
first declaration is `KotheConjecture` with no `variants` prefix). Happy to send one if
that is preferred.

## The mathematics is unaffected

**This is a defect in the formalization only, and a cosmetic one.** The Köthe conjecture
is untouched; the declaration is not false and not vacuous, and it is a correct
statement of formulation 6. In the four-coordinate sense: (1) the underlying conjecture
is untouched and open; (2) no formal solution exists; (3) the *docstring* is unfaithful
while the code is faithful; (4) what the declaration literally asserts is right, just
with two unused binders attached. Only (3) is at issue.

## Relationship to the C₅[K₄] campaign

Found while auditing `research open` declarations in the `Wikipedia` collection for
faithfulness to their cited sources. Full derivation and the duplicate search:

https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/c5-k4/blob/d8a0c47da83203e1cd2c739b383f7a436435549f/results/expansion/live-search-2026-08-15/wikipedia-scan-A-L.md

## Source/status note

Wikipedia, *Köthe conjecture*, "Equivalent formulations", item 6, quoted above. The
Köthe conjecture is open. `git log` on this file shows only formatting and
classical-reasoning chores since the file was created, so the docstring has said this
since the beginning; `matrixOver_KotherRadical` returns no issue or PR hits.

## AI assistance disclosure

This report was prepared with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) for the source audit and
drafting. The submitter reviewed the declaration, the source text, and the suggested
repair, and takes responsibility for the submission.

title: Extended Riemann Hypothesis (ERH) is false as currently stated
body:
### Describe the misformalization
The ERH statement at https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/60d13721bee9c49a21ee6510e2cf924637e47725/FormalConjectures/Millenium/RiemannHypothesis.lean#L127 can prove `False` with the following example. The problem is that Mathlib's `NumberField.dedekindZeta` has not been extended to the entire complex plane, thus producing junk zeros.

### Trivial proof/disproof
```lean
import Mathlib

--- The following is taken from FormalConjectures/Millenum/RiemannHypothesis.Lean
def IsInCriticalStrip (s : ℂ) : Prop :=
  0 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1


def trivialZeros (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] : Set ℤ :=
  by
    classical
    exact if NumberField.IsTotallyReal K then { -2 * n | (n : ℕ) } else Set.Iic 0

theorem extended_riemann_hypothesis_dedekindZeta (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] (s : ℂ)
    (hs : NumberField.dedekindZeta K s = 0)
    (hs_nontrivial : s ∉ Int.cast '' trivialZeros K)
    (hs_ne_one : s ≠ 1) :
    s.re = 1 / 2 := by
  sorry
--- end of FormalConjectures/Millenum/RiemannHypothesis.Lean snippet

noncomputable def idealEquiv : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ℚ) ≃o Ideal ℤ := RingEquiv.idealComapOrderIso Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.symm

noncomputable def idealSubtypeEquiv (b : ℕ) : { I : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers ℚ) // Ideal.absNorm I = b } ≃ { I : Ideal ℤ // Ideal.absNorm I = b } := by
  refine idealEquiv.subtypeEquiv ?_
  intro a
  congrm ?_ = _
  simp only [Ideal.absNorm_apply, Submodule.cardQuot, idealEquiv, RelIso.coe_fn_toEquiv,
    RingEquiv.idealComapOrderIso_apply, Ideal.comap_symm]
  have : RingHomSurjective Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toRingHom := ⟨Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.surjective⟩
  rw [show Ideal.map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv a = Submodule.map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toRingHom.toSemilinearMap a from Ideal.map_eq_submodule_map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toRingHom _]
  rw [show (Submodule.map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toRingHom.toSemilinearMap a).toAddSubgroup = a.toAddSubgroup.map Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.toAddEquiv from rfl]
  symm
  apply AddSubgroup.index_map_equiv (Submodule.toAddSubgroup a)

theorem card_ideal (b : ℕ) : Nat.card { I : Ideal ℤ // Ideal.absNorm I = b } = 1 := by
  rw [Nat.card_eq_one_iff_exists]
  refine ⟨⟨Ideal.span {(b : ℤ)}, by simp⟩, ?_⟩
  intro ⟨y, hy⟩
  simp [← hy]

theorem dedekind_quarter : NumberField.dedekindZeta ℚ (1 / 4 : ℂ) = 0 := by
  simp_rw [NumberField.dedekindZeta, LSeries, LSeries.term]
  apply tsum_eq_zero_of_not_summable
  simp_rw [fun b ↦ Nat.card_congr (idealSubtypeEquiv b), card_ideal]
  suffices ¬Summable fun (b : ℕ) => (1 / ↑b ^ (1 / 4 : ℂ) : ℂ) by
    convert this using 3 with b
    split_ifs with h
    · simp [h]
    simp
  rw [Complex.summable_one_div_nat_cpow]
  norm_num

theorem false : False := by
  have h := extended_riemann_hypothesis_dedekindZeta ℚ (1 / 4) dedekind_quarter (by 
    simp only [one_div, Set.mem_image, not_exists, not_and]
    intro x _ h
    obtain h := congr(4 * $h)
    simp at h
    norm_cast at h
    grind)
  simp at h

```

### Suggested fix
A proper definition that extends `NumberField.dedekindZeta` to the entire complex plane needs to be introduced first.
